title: SCRBench: Beyond Equivalence Checking for Semantic Change Reasoning in Code
abstract: arXiv:2610.41562v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Understanding how code changes affect program semantics is a core aspect of code reasoning in language models. It is commonly evaluated by asking whether two programs are semantically equivalent, but a yes/no answer does not reveal whether a model knows which code change caused a semantic difference, or which sequence of code changes produced the modified program. We study two tasks that ask these questions directly, diagnosing semantic change and reconstructing sequences of code changes, alongside detecting semantic equivalence. We build SCRBench, 67,658 Python program pairs generated by applying sequences of code changes that preserve or alter program semantics, and evaluate five language models on a stratified subset of 4,500 pairs. Detecting semantic equivalence exposes weaker models, whose accuracy declines as changes accumulate, but the strongest models remain near the ceiling. translated_title: SCRBench：超越等价性检查的代码语义变化推理
translated_abstract: 理解代码变化如何影响程序语义是语言模型代码推理的核心方面。这一能力通常通过询问两个程序是否语义等价来评估，但简单的“是/否”回答无法揭示模型是否知道是哪次代码更改导致了语义差异，也无法揭示是哪一序列的代码更改产生了修改后的程序。我们研究了两个直接提出这些问题的任务——诊断语义变化和重构代码更改序列——并结合语义等价性检测进行研究。我们构建了SCRBench，其中包含67,658对Python程序，这些程序对是通过应用保留或改变程序语义的代码更改序列生成的，并在4,500对的分层抽样子集上评估了五个语言模型。检测语义等价性暴露了较弱模型的不足，其准确率随着更改数量的累积而下降，但最强的模型仍接近性能上限。诊断语义变化则揭示了……
tldr: 该论文提出SCRBench基准，通过诊断语义变化和重构代码更改序列这两项新任务，超越了传统的语义等价性“是/否”判断，从而更深入地评估语言模型对代码语义变化的真实理解能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SCRBench, a benchmark of 67,658 Python program pairs that goes beyond yes/no equivalence checking by proposing two new tasks—diagnosing semantic change and reconstructing sequences of code changes—to deeply assess language models' reasoning about how code changes affect program semantics.
